title: Wexler and Ertegun as a producing team
summary: Matassa describes Jerry Wexler and Ahmet Ertegun as a great team who fought over ideas then settled, with Ertegun the stronger, major partner; Lew Chudd is called a cynic.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: John, Jerry Wexler, or Lou Chud, something like that?

No, no, no. They were, they were, they were more, well, Chud was a, was an eternal cynic. But, but Wexler was, you know, New York, Jew turned atheist. And, and hard, sharp, experienced, you know, all of the things Jerry Wexler is.

You know. And I don't mean to demean him by that, although it's okay. That, that was what he brought to the room. So, you didn't have to tell Ahmed Erdogan, for instance, or Jerry Wexler what to do, or suggest anything. And, of course, I would always, I always suggest the things. I always tell you, I make a suggestion once and then never repeat it. Because I learned that's the best way to deal with it. But, but they were, they were a great team, incidentally. One of the few where they'd fight like dogs about something. Do it this way, do it that way. You know, change it. And then somewhere along the way, one or the other would say, okay, your way. And that was the end of it. There was no more. Like at the end of the session, yeah, we should have done, you know, that. Right. I never heard that. Now, maybe they did it back home when they heard the tapes. I don't know. But I'll say that. I appreciated that in them. And, and since I'm not a Jerry Wexler fan, I would presume there was Ahmed who brought that to the thing. Besides, Ahmed was a very, how would you say, but very strong individual. He is, I should say. Mm-hmm. In that, that he had certain ideas about things and, and, and that's what he wanted. But he would defer to, to, to Jerry or to an arranger or somebody if, if they said, you know, try to listen to this. And he said, yeah, that's it. You know, good. Go with it.
And he would, he was the major partner. They were, they were not equals.
You could tell that. I mean, it was obvious. Yeah, oh yeah.
It was obvious. Oh, all the time. Yeah. All the time.
